description: This file defines various HTTP authentication security classes for FastAPI, including basic, bearer, and digest schemes, as well as credential data models.

classes.name: HTTPBasicCredentials
classes.description: Data model containing username and password for HTTP Basic authentication.

classes.name: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
classes.description: Data model containing scheme and credentials for HTTP authorization headers.

classes.name: HTTPBase
classes.description: Base security class providing common functionality for HTTP authentication schemes.

classes.name: HTTPBasic
classes.description: Implements HTTP Basic authentication scheme, handling credential parsing and header creation.

classes.name: HTTPBearer
classes.description: Implements HTTP Bearer token scheme, handling header extraction and validation.

classes.name: HTTPDigest
classes.description: Stub for HTTP Digest authentication scheme, currently for OpenAPI integration but not fully implemented.

methods.name: dict[str,str] make_authenticate_headers(self)
methods.description: Creates WWW-Authenticate headers for unauthorized responses.

methods.name: HTTPException make_not_authenticated_error(self)
methods.description: Generates an HTTP 401 Unauthorized exception with appropriate headers.

methods.name: Optional[HTTPBasicCredentials] __call__( self, request: Request )
methods.description: Asynchronously extracts and returns credentials from request headers, raising errors if authentication fails or optional.

                " ), ] = None, auto_error: Annotated[ bool, Doc( "
                By default, if the HTTP Bearer token is not provided (in an
                `Authorization` header), `HTTPBearer` will automatically cancel the
                request and send the client an error.

                If `auto_error` is set to `False`, when the HTTP Bearer token
                is not available, instead of erroring out, the dependency result will
                be `None`.

                This is useful when you want to have optional authentication.

                It is also useful when you want to have authentication that can be
                provided in one of multiple optional ways (for example, in an HTTP
                Bearer token or in a cookie).
                " ), ] = True, )
